title: One Host registry and one browser half for connector accounts
summary: One host registry (`ctx.connectorAccounts`) holds every connector account, whether it lives in a vendor command-line tool or in an OAuth grant held by the MCP manager. The host decides phase, status text, buttons and confirmations; the browser only displays them and opens the authorization page.
firstReason: The host already decides everything the page shows, which is exactly the shape server-rendered HTML wants, and registration that returns a disposer maps onto a cordis service. Only the browser half changes form, to a template, under DH-ADR-3.

title: Share Host preferences with every authenticated browser
summary: Every authenticated browser reads and writes the same host settings store; whether the page is loopback or remote no longer selects a different store. Only the Open configuration file button is hidden on non-loopback pages, as a presentation choice.
firstReason: Authentication is the identity boundary and locality is not, so a remote user must not lose preferences on reload. Host-stored preferences are also the natural model for a server-rendered UI.
